lines.text: I ranked 6 tools for building a trading strategy from S to F, so you don't have to.
Quant trading just means trading with rules and data instead of your gut.
And yes, I am biased because we built one.
Asking chat GPT what to buy.
F tier.
You're just getting an opinion that nobody has actually tested.
Excel.
D tier.
You can test a strategy on past prices in a spreadsheet, but one wrong sell and your test is secretly using tomorrow's price to make today's trade.
Your results look amazing, but they're fake.
Meta trader.
C tier.
It's popular for Forex, which is trading currencies like the dollar and the euro.
But to build a bot that trades for you, it needs to learn its own coding language.
Trading view.
B tier.
Really good charts and it can test strategies on past prices.
But to do that, you need to learn its coding language.
Pinescript.
Quant connect.
A tier.
Very powerful for testing strategies, but you have to write real code in Python or C-sharp.
Notice the pattern?
Everything from C to A wants you to be a programmer.
Cube.
S tier.
You describe the idea in plain English.
It turns it into exact rules, tests them on past prices and runs it.
No code required.
The hard part of trading should be the idea, not learning how to code.
Disagree?
Drop your tier list in the comments or comment cube and I'll send you the full breakdown.

notes: **Recreating:** our own M05 · https://www.instagram.com/reel/DerwxsIzyeX/ · M05's rhythm, cut to about 40s: one tool every 3–4s, each tool = name → tier → one short reason; the tier word said on its own ("F tier.") is an edit beat, the board fills one row on it; one short screen insert per tool; big text on "Full disclosure" and "MADE UP"; the board drops in on "so you don't have to".

**Layout:** M05's, reused as is (it's our own video). Talking head full frame; the tier board (A2) fixed in the top third (1080×640) and filling in; screen inserts replace the board in the top third for 1.5–4s, then the board comes back. Captions 2–4 words, M05's style ("TQX Captions" preset, key word on the navy highlight box), chest height (y = 1380).

**Times** are estimates at Joshua's pace (3.2 words a second, about 40s; 130 words). Re-time to the real take. Cuts are faster than M05's: keep every insert short and land each row exactly on its tier letter.

notes: **Presenter:** Joshua. One person, one list, in video order.

**Before recording anything:** the Qube team connects Qube to Claude on Joshua's laptop (same setup as J022) and he has a Qube login. Don't show any install commands, API keys, emails, account names or file paths. Every chatbot recording is on Joshua's own accounts, logged in, with notifications off.

**Reuse from M05:** the tier board, M05's big-text style (used for A3 with new words) and the caption style are M05's own. Duplicate them from the M05 CapCut project and swap only the logos, names and the A3 words. If the M05 project isn't available, build them from the specs below.
**Short video (about 40s):** every insert is on screen for 1.5–4s. Record each one as below, the editor speeds it up and keeps only the best few seconds.

rows.how: 1. Phone vertical (9:16), eye level, office lights on, lock focus and exposure, mic in hand like M05. 2. Frame head and chest in the lower two thirds, leaving the top third (640px) clear above his head for the board. 3. Record the hook twice, clean. 4. Record lines 1–9 in one take, fast, no gaps between tools. Say each tier word on its own with a short beat after it: "F tier." "D tier." 5. Move the phone in close and record "See the problem?" three times.

1. Get each logo from the company's own press or brand page: ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity, Claude, Qube (Qube from the TQX team). 2. Canva, 1080×640 transparent: the six logos in one row, top-left, each 90×90, 20px apart, in this order: ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity, Claude, Qube. 3. Export PNG.

1. Duplicate M05's board. Spec if rebuilding: 1080×640, background #0B0F14, six rows top to bottom S, A, B, C, D, F, each 96px high with 8px gaps; a 64×64 rounded letter tile on the left (S #F472B6, A #FB923C, B #FACC15, C #4ADE80, D #60A5FA, F #A78BFA, letter white Inter Bold 40px); row body #1A1F27; logo 56×56 after the tile; name right-aligned, Inter Bold 36px white. 2. 1. Phone, X app, logged in, notifications off. 2. Start the phone's screen recording. 3. On the home feed, hold 1s, then tap the Grok button. 4. Type exactly: `What are people saying about Apple stock today?` 5. Send. Record until the answer has 4–5 lines on screen. Hold 2s. Stop. **CHECK: no username, profile photo of a real person, "buy"/"sell" call or price target readable in the answer. If any is, blur it in the edit.**

rows.how: 1. Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks showing, https://www.perplexity.ai logged in. 2. Start a screen recording. 3. Type exactly: `What moved the S&P 500 this week?` 4. Press Enter. Record until the answer is done and its numbered sources are on screen. Hold 3s on the sources. 5. Screenshot the answer with the sources showing. **CHECK: the numbered source markers ([1], [2]…) or source cards must be readable. If Perplexity hides them, open the Sources tab and record that.**
rows.file: J028_A7_perplexity.mp4 · 1920×1080 · up to 20s (the edit uses about 2s) · plus J028_A7_sources.png

rows.how: 1. Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks showing, https://claude.ai logged in, a new chat. 2. Start a screen recording. 3. Type exactly, don't paste: `Write Python code for a strategy that buys the S&P 500 when it drops 2% in a day.` 4. Press Enter. Record until the code block is finished. Hold 2s on the code. **CHECK: stop the recording before Claude runs anything or shows any result. Only the code is on screen.**
rows.file: J028_A8_claude_code.mp4 · 1920×1080 · up to 30s (the edit uses about 2s, sped up)

rows.what: Claude connected to Qube, the strategy typed
rows.how: 1. Terminal app, dark theme, font 22, full screen. 2. Start a screen recording. 3. Type `claude`, press Enter. 4. Hold 2s on the screen that shows Qube is connected. 5. Type exactly, by hand, don't paste: `Using Qube, build a strategy that buys the S&P 500 when it drops 2% in a day. Sell once it's up 2% from where I bought, or if it falls another 3%. Test it on the last five years.` 6. Press Enter. Keep recording into A10. **CHECK: no email, key, file path or account name on screen at any point.**
rows.file: J028_A9_claude_qube.mp4 · 1920×1080 · up to 40s (the edit uses about 2.5s, sped up)

rows.what: Qube builds it, the backtest, every trade
rows.how: 1. Keep recording from A9 until Claude says the strategy is built and tested in Qube. 2. Open the strategy in Qube (Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%). 3. Record the backtest result for 3s. 4. Open the list of every trade and scroll top to bottom in about 3s. Hold 2s. 5. Screenshot the result and the trade list. **CHECK: the dates must cover five years or less (Qube tests on up to five years of real price data). If it ran longer, tell Mark before the edit.** **CHECK: don't change any number Qube shows; nothing is spoken about it. If the result shows no trades, stop and send Mark the screenshot.**
rows.file: J028_A10_qube.mp4 · 1920×1080 · up to 30s (the edit uses about 4s, sped up) · plus J028_A10_result.png, _trades.png
